question: A Cisco UCS user called 'Employee1' accidentally changed the boot policy of the Cisco UCS server at the Cisco UCS Manager root level. This change impacted all service profiles, and their storage connectivity was lost. The system administrator wants to prevent this issue from recurring in the future. The new security policy mandates that access must be restricted up to the organization level and prevent other users from modifying root policies. Which action must be taken to meet these requirements?
options: Modify the privilege level assigned to the user
Assign users to a specific Cisco UCS locale
Assign the user 'Employee1' the network-operator role
Define a custom user role and assign it to users
theory: Cisco UCS Manager's RBAC model separates what a user can do (privileges/roles) from where they can do it (locale/organization scope). Restricting an account so it can only manage a specific sub-organization — and cannot touch root-level policies that would impact every service profile inheriting from root — requires assigning that user to a locale bound to the appropriate organization, rather than changing their role's privilege level or giving them a broader built-in role like network-operator, neither of which limits scope to an organization. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 12 — Cisco UCS Manager Administration, Locales and Organizational Permissions)
